[RS_SOMEIP_00032]
SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting float data
types ⌈
Description:
SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting float data types kown as single
and double (defined in IEEE 754 [3] as binary32 and binary64)
Rationale:
For the specification of a serialization algorithm of SOME/IP, a set of basic data
types needs to be supported by SOME/IP.
Use Case:
Communication of c-data types
AppliesTo:
FO
Dependencies:
–
Supporting
Material:
–
⌋(RS_Main_00280)
[RS_SOMEIP_00033] SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting structured
data types ⌈
Description:
SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting structured data types which can
consist of one or multiple structured data types of fixed or variable size and/or
primitive data types.
Rationale:
For the specification of a serialization algorithm of SOME/IP, a set of data types
needs to be supported by SOME/IP.
Use Case:
Consistent communication of more than one primitive data type.
AppliesTo:
FO
Dependencies:
–
Supporting
Material:
–
⌋(RS_Main_00280)
[RS_SOMEIP_00034] SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting union data
types ⌈
Description:
SOME/IP protocol shall support transporting union data types where the
concrete data type is determined during execution.
Rationale:
For the specification of a serialization algorithm of SOME/IP, a set of data types
needs to be supported by SOME/IP.
Use Case:
Communication of data with the possibility to choose representation
dynamically.
AppliesTo:
FO
Dependencies:
–
Supporting
Material:
–
⌋(RS_Main_00280)
